summary: Attachment custody (photos, stickers, voice notes) can now be stored in RustFS, an S3-compatible object store, instead of the local filesystem.
detail: [media.rustfs] is a new, off-by-default section: enabling it (endpoint, bucket, credential env vars) swaps FilesystemBlobStore for RustfsBlobStore in the composition root, reusing the same BlobCipher encryption-at-rest and the same BlobStore port, so nothing about the ingest pipeline changes. RustFS already runs in this deployment for the drop link-shortener's own artifacts, so enabling this adds no new container. A misconfigured or unreachable RustFS falls back to the filesystem store rather than crashing the daemon or disabling custody.
limitations: Ships OFF. Enabling it in the real deployment, and migrating the blobs already on the filesystem, are separate operator decisions not made by this change.
No lifecycle/retention behavior is added for either backend — the operator decision DEC-43 already deferred.
